title: Zambia Catch Up caregiver attendance-information messaging: test routing decision

feasible_options.feasibility_condition: Reliable child-level data can cheaply distinguish school absence, present-but-missed Catch Up, session non-delivery, and Catch Up attendance.

feasible_options.label: Do not test messaging yet

feasible_options.feasibility_condition: Not supported by current canonical evidence.

routing_recommendation.recommendation: Test, do not scale: allocate one bounded Zambia Catch Up implementation-comparison slot to weekly caregiver information on school and Catch Up attendance only if low-incremental-cost child-level exposure data are available.
routing_recommendation.reason: Canonical P05 work identifies caregiver attendance-information messaging as the strongest candidate found in its bounded search while preserving major portability and mechanism uncertainty.

closest_same_package_research_evidence.setting: seven low-income schools in Santiago, Chile
closest_same_package_research_evidence.use_limit: Research denominator only; not a Zambia budget estimate.

mechanism_close_african_evidence.reported_cost: about R1.01 per child per week
mechanism_close_african_evidence.use_limit: Mechanism-close but lacks downstream learning outcomes and is not a portable Zambia cost denominator.

zambia_local_feasibility_evidence.intervention: parent-facing SMS plus monthly-meeting early-reading package
zambia_local_feasibility_evidence.use_limit: Supports local low-tech parent outreach feasibility with learning effects, but bundles different content and does not isolate attendance/exposure.

items: Current evidence does not support a portable Zambia cost-effectiveness estimate for caregiver attendance messaging.
Chile US$10.86/student-year, Cape Town R1.01/child-week, and Zambia US$20-22/child use incompatible settings, packages, currencies, accounting scopes, and outcome mechanisms.
Current evidence does not establish that messaging is more cost-effective than standard Catch Up or every alternative exposure intervention.

uncertainties_and_contrary_evidence: The Chile effect may not transfer to Zambia Catch Up because institutional context and administrative data systems differ.
Cape Town evidence is mechanism-close but lacks learning outcomes and comes from a master's thesis.
The Zambia evidence changes home reading directly and includes monthly meetings, so it does not identify attendance as the mechanism.
Messaging cannot fix session non-delivery or other non-family-controllable causes of missed exposure.
Additional attendance matters only when Catch Up sessions are actually delivered with adequate instructional quality.
Current evidence is insufficient for national rollout or a portable Zambia cost-effectiveness claim.
adoption_constraints: child-level school and Catch Up attendance data quality
ability to distinguish absence from session non-delivery
caregiver phone ownership and number matching
Catch Up instructional quality and session availability

to_do_not_test: Zambia cannot cheaply distinguish school absence, present-but-missed Catch Up, and Catch Up non-delivery.
Micro-costing shows the information system is too expensive for a bounded mechanism test relative to plausible value.
after_pilot_downgrade_or_stop: Messaging improves recorded attendance but does not materially increase realized Catch Up sessions.
Added Catch Up exposure does not improve policy-relevant learning.
Implementation failures make caregiver information unreliable or poorly delivered.
toward_scale_consideration: A Zambia randomized pilot shows meaningful additional Catch Up exposure and downstream learning with a defensible incremental cost denominator and acceptable implementation burden.
Replication or operational evidence reduces portability uncertainty and supports persistence of effects.

arms: weekly caregiver information on school plus Catch Up attendance
primary_mechanism_outcomes: Catch Up attendance conditional on school presence
cost_outcomes: incremental cost per additional realized Catch Up session
